stem: What are subscriptions in arrears?

options.content: Subscriptions due for the year that members have not yet paid
options.rationale: Correct: they are earned but not yet received.

options.content: Subscriptions that members have paid for a future year
options.rationale: That describes subscriptions received in advance.

options.content: Subscriptions that the club has decided it will never collect
options.rationale: Those are irrecoverable subscriptions.

options.content: Subscriptions paid by the club to a national association
options.rationale: That is an expense of the club.

explanation: Arrears are subscriptions owing from members at the end of the period.

stem: How are subscriptions received in advance shown in the club's statement of financial position?

options.content: As a current liability
options.rationale: Correct: the club owes the members future membership.

options.content: As a current asset
options.rationale: Arrears, not advances, are current assets.

options.content: As part of the accumulated fund
options.rationale: They belong to the next period and are not yet income.

options.content: They are not shown
options.rationale: All balances at the year end appear in the statement.

explanation: An advance is an amount owed to members for a future period, a current liability.

stem: A club received subscriptions of US\$5,200. Arrears were US\$160 at the start and US\$220 at the end; there were no advances. What is the subscriptions income?

options.rationale: Closing arrears are added; opening arrears are deducted.
Arrears must be adjusted for.
Opening arrears must be deducted.

hints: Arrears at the end are earned but not received.

stem: A club writes off subscriptions of US\$90 as irrecoverable. How is this treated?

options.content: It is deducted from the subscriptions income
options.rationale: The income is found first; the loss is a separate expense.

options.content: It is an expense in the income and expenditure account
options.rationale: Correct: the amount will never be received, so it is a loss.

options.content: It is added to the accumulated fund
options.rationale: A loss reduces the fund; it never increases it.

options.content: It is ignored until the member leaves
options.rationale: Once it is known to be irrecoverable it must be written off.

explanation: A write-off is charged as an expense; the arrears are reduced by the same amount.
hints: Is the amount a gain or a loss?

stem: A club received subscriptions of US\$7,340 and wrote off US\$80 of arrears. Arrears were US\$260 at the start and US\$310 at the end; subscriptions in advance were US\$140 at the start and US\$90 at the end. What is the subscriptions income, found as the balancing figure of the subscriptions account?

options.rationale: The write-off has been deducted instead of added to the credit side.
The advances and write-off are missing.
The advance at the end is added instead of deducted.

hints: Total the credit side and deduct the opening arrears and closing advance.

stem: A member pays this year's fee in the previous December. How is the amount treated this year?

options.content: It is part of the arrears at the start, so it is deducted
options.rationale: Arrears are amounts not yet received.

options.content: It is ignored because the cash was received last year
options.rationale: It is income of this year.

options.content: It is an opening advance, so it adds to this year's income
options.rationale: Correct: it was received last year but belongs to this year.

options.content: It is an expense of this year and reduces the surplus
options.rationale: Receipts are never expenses.

explanation: Opening advances are added when finding the income of the year to which they relate.
hints: Which year does the payment belong to?

stem: The balance of the subscriptions account is transferred to the income and expenditure account. On which side of the subscriptions account does this balancing figure appear?

options.content: The credit side
options.rationale: The cash received is on the credit side.

options.content: It appears on both sides
options.rationale: It is a single figure.

options.content: It does not appear in the account
options.rationale: The account always shows the transfer.

options.content: The debit side
options.rationale: Correct: the income account is credited in the income and expenditure account, so subscriptions is debited.

explanation: The subscriptions account is debited and the income and expenditure account is credited with the income.
hints: Double entry: the other account is credited.

stem: A club has 150 members who each pay US\$48 a year. Cash received was US\$7,100, arrears were US\$250 at the start and US\$300 at the end, and subscriptions received in advance were US\$100 at the end (none at the start). The treasurer expects the income to equal members × fee. What does the check show?

options.content: The income from the account equals members × fee, so the records are correct
options.rationale: The two figures differ.

options.content: The income from the account is US\$150 above members × fee, so it is overstated
options.rationale: It is lower, not higher.

options.content: The check cannot be made because advances are received at the year end
options.rationale: Advances are included in the calculation.

options.content: The income (US\$7,050) is US\$150 below members × fee, so a payment may be missing
options.rationale: Correct: the difference suggests an error or a member who has not been charged.

explanation: Income = 7,100 + 300 − 250 − 100 = 7,050. Members × fee = 7,200. The 150 difference needs investigating.
hints: Calculate the income from the account and compare with 150 × 48.

stem: Subscriptions in arrears at the end of the year are added to the cash received when finding the income of the year.
explanation: True. They are earned in the year but not yet received.

stem: Irrecoverable subscriptions written off are deducted from the subscriptions income.
explanation: False. They are an expense; the income is found with the write-off on the credit side of the account.

stem: Match each subscription balance with its treatment at the year end.

right.content: Expense in the income and expenditure account
Balancing figure of the subscriptions account

explanation: Each balance has a defined place in the statements.

stem: Complete the statements about the subscriptions account.

payload.template: Arrears at the end of the year are {{blank:a}} to the cash received. Subscriptions received in advance at the end of the year are {{blank:b}}. The balancing figure is transferred to the income and {{blank:c}} account.

explanation: Arrears are added, advances deducted, and the income goes to the income and expenditure account.

stem: Opening arrears US\$380, opening advance US\$120, closing arrears US\$440 and closing advance US\$90. Cash received was US\$9,260. Calculate the subscriptions income for the year.
hints: Add the closing arrears and opening advance; deduct the opening arrears and closing advance.

stem: A club has 85 members who each pay US\$120 a year. Calculate the expected subscriptions income.

The subscriptions income for the year is US\$6,480. Arrears were US\$220 at the start and US\$300 at the end; advances were US\$95 at the start and US\$125 at the end; US\$60 was written off. Calculate the cash received from members.
hints: Rearrange: cash = income − write-off − closing arrears − opening advance + opening arrears + closing advance.

stem: At the end of the year a club has 38 members who have not paid their annual fee of US\$120. Calculate the subscriptions in arrears shown as a current asset.
Name the account of a club that finds the subscription income for the year by balancing.
explanation: The subscriptions account matches the cash received to the year.

stem: Explain why the cash received for subscriptions is not the same as the subscription income of the year.

points.description: Some members pay late (arrears) or early (advance), so cash and income fall in different years
Income belongs to the year in which it is earned (the accruals concept)
The subscriptions account adjusts the cash received for the opening and closing balances

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Some members pay late or early, so cash and income fall in different years. Income belongs to the year in which it is earned, so the cash received is adjusted for opening and closing arrears and advances in the subscriptions account.

explanation: One mark each for timing differences, the accruals concept and the adjustment.
hints: Think about members who pay late.

stem: State and explain how subscriptions in arrears and subscriptions received in advance are classified in the statement of financial position.

points.description: Arrears are a current asset, because the club expects to receive the money soon
Advances are a current liability, because the club owes members future membership
Both are shown at the end of the year at the amounts in the subscriptions account

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Arrears are a current asset because the club expects to receive the cash soon. Advances are a current liability because the club owes members future membership.

explanation: One mark each for the asset, the liability and the amounts.

stem: A club's subscriptions in arrears have risen from US\$300 to US\$1,200 over two years. Evaluate what this might mean and suggest an action.

points.description: More members are paying late, which may reduce cash for expenses
Some of the arrears may become irrecoverable and have to be written off
The club may have lost control of collection or members may be in difficulty
Action: send reminders and set a deadline after which membership lapses

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The rise shows more members are paying late, so cash is lower and some arrears may be written off. The club should send reminders and set a deadline after which membership lapses.

explanation: A balanced answer states the risks and a suitable action.

stem: Harare Golf Club has 262 members who each pay an annual subscription of US\$60. At 1 January 2025 subscriptions in arrears were US\$560 and subscriptions received in advance US\$230. During 2025 the club received US\$15,600 and wrote off US\$180 of arrears as irrecoverable. At 31 December 2025 arrears were US\$600 and subscriptions received in advance US\$330.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the subscriptions income for the year.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Prepare the subscriptions account for the year.

points.description: Debit: arrears b/d 560 and advance c/d 330
Debit: income and expenditure account 15,720 (own figure)
Credit: advance b/d 230, bank 15,600 and irrecoverable subscriptions 180
Credit: arrears c/d 600, with totals of 16,610 on both sides

answerSpec.modelAnswer:

| 31 Dec 2025 | Income and expenditure account | 15,720 | 31 Dec 2025 | Bank: subscriptions received | 15,600 |
| 31 Dec 2025 | Balance c/d: received in advance | 330 | 31 Dec 2025 | Irrecoverable subscriptions written off | 180 |
|  |  |  | 31 Dec 2025 | Balance c/d: arrears | 600 |

parts.explanation: The income is the balancing figure on the debit side.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Where is the balance of US\$600 carried down shown in the statement of financial position at 31 December 2025?

options.content: Current liabilities
options.rationale: Arrears are not owed by the club.

options.content: Accumulated fund
options.rationale: It is an asset, not part of the fund.

options.content: Non-current assets
options.rationale: It will be received within a year.

options.content: Current assets
options.rationale: Correct: arrears are owed to the club.

parts.explanation: Subscriptions in arrears are a current asset.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Use the number of members to check the income. Calculate members × annual fee.
parts.explanation: 262 × 60 = 15,720, which agrees with the income from the account.
parts.workedSolution: 1. 262 × 60 = 15,720, which agrees with the income from the account.

explanation: This item practises a full subscriptions account with a write-off.
hints: The write-off is on the credit side of the account.
The income is a balancing figure.

stem: Bulawayo Swimming Club had 200 members throughout the year ended 30 June 2026, each paying an annual fee of US\$48. At 1 July 2025 subscriptions in arrears were US\$480 and subscriptions received in advance US\$144. At 30 June 2026 arrears were US\$336 and advances US\$192. Arrears of US\$96 from members who had left were written off during the year. The treasurer lost the record of the cash received.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the subscriptions income for the year.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the cash received from members during the year.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Prepare the subscriptions account for the year.

points.description: Debit side: arrears b/d 480 and advance c/d 192
Credit side: advance b/d 144 and bank 9,696 (own figure)
Irrecoverable subscriptions written off 96
Arrears c/d 336
Income and expenditure account 9,600 as the balancing figure, totals agreeing at 10,272

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
**Subscriptions account for the year ended 30 June 2026**

| Date | Details | US\$ | Date | Details | US\$ |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: |
| 1 Jul 2025 | Balance b/d: arrears | 480 | 1 Jul 2025 | Balance b/d: received in advance | 144 |
| 30 Jun 2026 | Income and expenditure account | 9,600 | 30 Jun 2026 | Bank: subscriptions received | 9,696 |
| 30 Jun 2026 | Balance c/d: received in advance | 192 | 30 Jun 2026 | Irrecoverable subscriptions written off | 96 |
|  |  |  | 30 Jun 2026 | Balance c/d: arrears | 336 |
| | | **10,272** | | | **10,272** |

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Explain how the write-off of US\$96 is shown in the income and expenditure account.

points.description: It is an expense (irrecoverable subscriptions)
It is not deducted from the subscriptions income of 9,600

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The US\$96 is an expense in the income and expenditure account. It is not deducted from the subscriptions income of US\$9,600.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Suggest one reason for, and one effect of, the club having both arrears and advances at the year end.

points.description: Some members pay late and others pay early because there is no strict payment deadline
Cash received differs from income, so the treasurer must adjust to avoid misstating the surplus

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Some members pay late and some early because there is no strict deadline. The cash received therefore differs from income, so the treasurer must adjust for arrears and advances to avoid misstating the surplus.

parts.explanation: One mark for the reason and one for the effect.

explanation: This item practises working back from the income to the cash received and preparing the account.
hints: Work backwards from the income to the cash.
Check that both sides of the account agree.
